newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO growth seen driving Russia, Belarus closer.
newsitem.headline: NATO growth seen driving Russia, Belarus closer.

text.p: A senior Kremlin official suggested on Monday that unification between Russia and Belarus could be the best response to NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

Interfax news agency quoted Sergei Shakhrai, deputy head of the Kremlin administration, as saying that unification would meet Russia's strategic and economic interests and would add weight to Moscow's international authority.
Officially no merger has been proposed between the two neighbouring Slav states which signed an accord last April on closer economic and political ties.

But a top Kremlin official, speaking last month on condition of anonymity, said the Russian leadership was seriously considering its position over Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko's plan to hold a referendum in March on a possible union.

Lukashenko has made no secret of his desire to be as close to Russia as possible. He said in a Sunday television programme he enjoyed playing the role of "a junior brother" to Russian leader Boris Yeltsin.

"Shakhrai considers that the most effective answer to NATO's expansion eastwards would be real unification between Russia and Belarus," Interfax said. "He considers that 1997 gives unique possibilities for a Russian-Belarussian merger," it added.
Earlier on Monday a senior Kremlin official had suggested that unification between Russia and Belarus could be the best response to NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying in his letter to the hardline Lukashenko that the community had become a reality and further, serious steps should follow to bring the two former Soviet republics closer together.
